problems.title: Direct convolution cost
problems.statement: A 7 × 7 filter (R = 3) on a 2048 × 2048 FP32 image, naive kernel.
problems.solution: 49 FMAs and 49 loads per output; 206 M FMAs. Intensity against loads is 2 FLOPs per 4 bytes whatever the filter size: the loads must be shared.

parts.prompt: Global loads per output for R = 2?

problems.title: Idle threads
problems.statement: The "threads = input tile" design: (T + 2R)² threads load, T² compute.

parts.prompt: Fraction idle during compute for T = 16, R = 2, in %?

problems.solution: 36% and 23.4%: bigger tiles waste fewer threads, but blocks are capped at 1,024 threads.

problems.title: Shared memory per tile

parts.prompt: Blocks per SM by shared memory on the GW-1 (64 KB)?

problems.solution: 5,776 bytes (5,888 allocated): 11 blocks fit by shared memory, so another limit (threads) binds first.

problems.title: Separable filters

parts.prompt: The price of the separable version?
options: An intermediate image written and read once

problems.solution: 81 versus 18 FMAs, at the cost of one extra write and read of the intermediate image: worth it for large filters.

problems.title: Constant memory

parts.prompt: A warp where every lane reads F[k] for the same k…

options: serialises: constant memory broadcasts one address per cycle

hints: Constant cache: one address per warp per cycle.
problems.solution: Constant memory is ideal when all lanes read the same element, as in convolution's filter loop; divergent indices serialise.

problems.title: Halo traffic in 3-D
problems.statement: A 3-D convolution, R = 1, cubic tiles of T³ outputs.

parts.prompt: Smallest T with at most 1.25 loads per output?

problems.solution: (a) 1000/512 = 1.95. (b) T = 26: 17576 outputs per tile, far more than a block's 1,024 threads, so 3-D needs coarsening (Chapter 10.2).

problems.title: Ghost cells
problems.statement: A 5 × 5 filter on a 64 × 64 image with zero ghost cells.

parts.prompt: Outputs whose window reaches outside the image?

hints: Interior: outputs at least 2 from every edge.
problems.solution: 4,096 − 60² = 496 outputs need ghost cells. Branching for them diverges only in edge warps; loading zeros into the shared tile handles them without branches in the compute loop.

problems.title: When tiling doesn't show
problems.statement: In the simulator, tiling cut SM↔L2 sectors 12× but the time barely changed.

options: L2 already served the repeated reads, and L2 bandwidth wasn't the limit
Large images with long reuse distances

problems.solution: The cache absorbed the reuse; tiling pays when the cache can't (big working sets, 3-D) or when L2 bandwidth binds.
